newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina says GDP up 4.4 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Argentina says GDP up 4.4 pct in 1996.

text.p: Argentina's economy grew 4.4 percent in 1996 and 9.2 percent in the fourth quarter of the year, the Economy Ministry said Thursday in a report.
Gross domestic product had shrunk 4.6 percent in 1995 due to the recession unleashed by the Tequila crisis following the shock devaluation of the Mexican peso in December 1994.
"(With this growth) we recover a great part of the fall registered in 1995," the report said.

"Goods (output) in the fourth quarter of 1996 showed year-on-year growth of 12.1 percent, boosted by a very significant rise in the farming, mining, construction and manufacturing sectors," it said. Manufacturing activity in that period picked up 9.5 percent, according to the national statistics institute INDEC.
The Economy Ministry said goods and services together grew 6.8 percent in the fourth quarter.
The Economy Ministry also said it revised third-quarter GDP growth upwards to 6.7 percent from 6.6 percent.
(1) with import tax. (2) without financial items.
